package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a high-severity Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs. This can be exploited to access internal resources, perform denial of service, or chain with other vulnerabilities for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is present by default in affected versions and can be triggered without authentication, making the entire package version range dangerous in security-sensitive contexts.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when XML input is parsed by the library, e.g., during SAML authentication or metadata processing)
execution_context.file_location: core xmltooling library code (C++), specifically in the XML parsing and KeyInfo element handling logic

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML snippet, when processed by vulnerable xmltooling versions, causes the library to fetch and process the external URI specified in the RetrievalMethod. If the URI is attacker-controlled, it can be used to trigger SSRF, access internal resources, or deliver further payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Permitting arbitrary external URI resolution from untrusted XML input enables attackers to force the application to make network requests to internal or external systems, violating trust boundaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SAML/XML processing should not allow untrusted users to cause the server to fetch arbitrary URLs, especially without authentication or input validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may use RetrievalMethod to fetch trusted keys or metadata, but only from whitelisted or validated sources.
key_indicators: Unrestricted URI resolution in XML input
No validation or restriction on RetrievalMethod URI
Network requests triggered by parsing attacker-supplied XML

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits crafted SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo element with a RetrievalMethod URI pointing to an attacker-controlled or internal resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and attempts to resolve the URI.

attack_chain.action: The library makes a network request to the specified URI, potentially accessing internal services or fetching attacker-controlled data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can use SSRF to access restricted resources, exfiltrate data, or chain with other vulnerabilities (e.g., command injection) for further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from SAML or XML processing services
Resolution of external URIs specified in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements of XML input
Network requests to internal IPs or sensitive endpoints triggered by XML parsing
file_indicators: Presence of unpatched xmltooling library versions (<3.2.4)
SAML/XML logs showing external URI access in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains from SAML processing hosts
Requests to internal network resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254, localhost) initiated by SAML/XML parsing processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML and XML processing services for outbound network requests, especially those triggered during authentication or metadata parsing. Inspect logs for KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements referencing external or non-whitelisted URIs. Use file integrity monitoring to identify unpatched xmltooling library versions. Employ network egress controls to block unauthorized outbound requests from authentication gateways and review for signs of SSRF exploitation.
